drills.title: Typed variables
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines and pick the right type for each blank so the program prints the goal output. The two assignments can go in either order. One line does not belong.
drills.explain: Java needs the type in front of the name. 120.5 has decimals, so it needs a double, and so does qty * price (an int times a double is a double). A variable must be declared before it is used.

drills.title: Parse and format
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: Integer.parseInt turns text into an int. String.format builds a text from a pattern (%d whole number, %s text). With text on one side, + glues instead of adding: "5" + 3 is "53".

drills.title: Copies, text and formats
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: copy got its own 3, so changing qty later does not change it. "5" + 3 is text (53) but 5 + 3 is a number (8). In %-8s the - means left-aligned in 8 characters, %5d right-aligns the number in 5.

drills.title: A decimal in an int
drills.prompt: The program crashes while it runs. Click the line that crashes, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: Integer.parseInt only accepts whole numbers, so "12.5" throws NumberFormatException. A price with decimals needs a double and Double.parseDouble. Casting with (int) would silently cut the .5 off.

drills.title: Review the AI's order slip
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this order slip with Scanner. It compiles, but tick the real problems (there are two).

issues.text: nextLine() right after nextInt() returns an empty text, so item is blank
issues.why: nextInt() leaves the end-of-line behind and nextLine() reads just that. Call in.nextLine() once to discard it, or read every line with nextLine() and parse it.

issues.text: The total is printed unformatted, so money can show as 1048.5 or 1048.4999999
issues.why: Format money with printf("%.2f") / String.format, so it always has two decimals.

non_issues.text: qty * price is a compile error because qty is an int
non_issues.why: An int is widened to double automatically, so the product is a double.

non_issues.text: The import must be placed inside the class
non_issues.why: imports go at the very top of the file, before the class.

non_issues.text: String item must be written with var
non_issues.why: var is optional. An explicit type is fine and often clearer.

drills.explain: Scanner's nextInt/nextLine leftover-newline problem is the classic bug in generated console programs, and money printed straight from a double is rarely what you want.
